cards.explanation: The disciples rebuked the people who brought the children. Those people brought the little ones so Jesus could place His hands on them, and a rebuke is what they got. I think those folks were not expecting that at all.

The kingdom of God belongs to people like these children. Jesus says, “For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.” That's the reason He gives for not hindering the little children. The disciples had rebuked those who brought them, and Jesus tells them not to hinder them.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.” Never, friends. That's how plainly He puts it.

The answer is True, and what a scene. After all those words, Jesus took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them. The people had brought the children for Him to place His hands on them, and He did that and blessed them too.

The man asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. He ran up, knelt, and asked, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” I think he was serious about it. A man who runs up and kneels doesn't look like he's asking a small question to me.

The man says he has kept all of them since his youth. His words are, “Teacher, all these I have kept from my youth.” That's quite a claim, and the text gives no hint that Jesus argues with him about it. Next comes Jesus looking at him with love.
The word is poor. Jesus tells the man to sell everything he owns and give to the poor, and then he will have treasure in heaven. It's a big ask, friends, and Jesus says it looking at him with love.
The man goes away in sorrow, and it's a heavy moment. The text says the man was saddened by these words and went away in sorrow. Jesus had just invited him to come follow Him. I think this one hurts.
The word is wealth. The man went away in sorrow because he had great wealth. Jesus had just told him to sell everything he owned. That's a lot to hold in your hands and hear that.
The answer is True. The text says the disciples were amazed at His words. Jesus had just said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!” I bet that one landed hard.

Jesus says a camel passing through the eye of a needle is easier. His words are, “It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.” A camel is a big animal and a needle's eye is tiny. Jesus is making it clear this is hard.
The disciples ask one another, “Who then can be saved?” If a camel and a needle made them nervous, I get it, friends. Jesus has an answer coming for them.

The word is God. Jesus says, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.” The disciples asked who can be saved, and Jesus points them to God. That's a good answer to hang onto.

Jesus says anyone who leaves home or family or fields for His sake and the gospel will receive a hundredfold in the present age. He lists houses, brothers and sisters, mothers, children and fields. And in the age to come, eternal life.

The answer is False. Jesus says the hundredfold comes “…houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions…” The promise is real, and so is the part about persecutions. Jesus tells them both.

Many who are first will be last. Jesus says, “But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.” Notice the word many, friends. That flips how people usually think about who's in front.
